items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: The mention of Reverend Leo Humphrey occurs in the [INTERVIEWER]'s monologue describing a future radio segment ('We're going to assemble a panel... Reverend Leo Humphrey...'). The interviewee, Johnny Wiggs, does not respond to this specific mention with any personal anecdote or confirmation of a rel

ctx.x: Yeah, he caught it raw. He was on Canal Street. I remember that. It should be known that Tom Brown was the first white man to take jazz out of New Orleans, his band. Oh, yeah. Up to Chicago, yeah. Up to Chicago, yeah. All the way up there, and then on to New York. That's where they call him that dirty old name of a jazz player. Before getting off, I wanted to ask you, since I'm in my 50s, too, I mean, I do a little composing, but I can't adapt to rock and roll. Perhaps I'm too old. But is there any market for…

It's really hard now. The whole music scene has changed so much. That's right. Okay, we certainly do appreciate your comments. Thank you. Nice talking to you. Thank you for calling. Let's talk it over and talking it over with Johnny Wiggs of Johnny Wiggs and his New Orleans Kings and Mr. Dick Allen of Tulane University's Jazz Archives. The number to call? All, well, yeah, 523-2404. There's one line open, the one we've just vacated, but it won't be open very long, I should imagine. You've heard of the Industrial…
This is WTIS 690 in New Orleans, Louisiana.
